column1: obliterate§Snow obliterated the path within twenty minutes.§二十分钟内，雪就把小路盖得**无影无踪**。
oblivion§He worked in happy oblivion of the deadline.§他**浑然不觉**截止日期，愉快地工作着。
oblivious§Oblivious to the rain, the crew finished the roof.§**不顾**大雨，工人们把屋顶做完了。
obnoxious§The smell was obnoxious and entirely harmless.§这种气味**令人厌恶**，却完全无害。
obscure§A cloud obscured the summit for the whole afternoon.§一片云整个下午**遮住**了山顶。
obsequious§Obsequious to superiors, he was brutal to everyone else.§他对上级**谄媚**，对其他人却粗暴。
observable§An observable change in behaviour beats a reported one.§**可观察**到的行为变化胜过口头报告的。
obsession§An obsession becomes a discipline when someone else can use it.§当别人也能用上时，**执迷**就成了一门学问。
obsolete§Skills go obsolete faster than the tools that use them.§技能**过时**的速度比使用它们的工具还快。
obstinacy§Obstinacy about the wrong thing is how projects die.§在错误的事情上**固执**，项目就是这么死的。
obstinate§An obstinate cough kept her out of the choir all winter.§一场**顽固的**咳嗽让她整个冬天都没能参加合唱。
obstreperous§An obstreperous parrot made the reading room impossible.§一只**吵闹的**鹦鹉让阅览室没法待了。
obstruction§Obstruction of the inquiry added two years to the case.§对调查的**妨碍**让这个案子多拖了两年。
obtrusive§The microphone was obtrusive and the sound was excellent.§麦克风很**碍眼**，音质却极好。
obtuse§An obtuse angle looks larger than it measures.§**钝角**看起来比实际度数还大。
occasionally§Occasionally the method fails, and those cases teach the most.§这个方法**偶尔**会失效，而那些情形教人最多。
occlusion§A warm front occlusion brought rain for three days.§暖锋的**锢囚**带来了三天的雨。
odoriferous§Odoriferous plants were grown along the path on purpose.§这条小径旁有意种了**散发香气**的植物。
officious§An officious footnote explains what the reader already knows.§**多此一举**的脚注解释着读者早已知道的东西。
offset§The gain in speed is offset by a loss in accuracy.§速度上的提升被精度的损失**抵消**了。
omission§Omission of a source is an error; concealment is not.§**漏掉**出处是错误，隐瞒则不是。
onerous§An onerous duty performed cheerfully is still onerous.§愉快地履行的**繁重**职责，仍然是繁重的。
onset§The onset of symptoms was sudden and the recovery slow.§症状**发作**突然，康复却缓慢。
opacity§Opacity in the accounts is a decision, not an accident.§账目的**不透明**是刻意的，不是偶然的。
opinionated§An opinionated introduction can ruin a neutral anthology.§一篇**立场鲜明**的导言可能毁掉一部中立的选集。
opportune§There is no opportune moment to deliver news like that.§这种消息没有什么**合适的时机**去传达。
opportunism§What looked like strategy was opportunism with good timing.§看似战略的东西，是时机恰好的**机会主义**。
opportunist§An opportunist reads the room faster than anyone.§**投机者**比谁都更快读懂场面。
opportunistic§An opportunistic species fills any gap within one season.§**机会主义的**物种一季之内就能填满任何空隙。
opposition§The opposition's amendment was adopted almost word for word.§**反对**党的修正案几乎被逐字采纳。
opt§She opted out of the scheme and explained why in writing.§她**选择**退出这个计划，并书面说明了理由。
optimism§Optimism about a schedule is not a plan.§对进度的**乐观**不是计划。
opulent§The opulent years left debts the lean years had to pay.§**丰裕的**岁月留下的债，要由清贫的岁月来还。
orb§The orb and sceptre appear on coins of that reign.§那个朝代的钱币上有**宝球**和权杖。
originality§Originality is often just an unusual pair of sources.§**独创性**往往只是一对不寻常的来源。
ornamentation§Ornamentation was stripped in 1962 and regretted ever since.§一九六二年剥去了这些**装饰**，此后一直令人惋惜。
ornate§An ornate signature on a plain document is a warning sign.§朴素文件上一个**华丽的**签名是个警示。
ossify§A method ossifies when nobody remembers why it was chosen.§当没人记得为何选择某种方法时，它就**僵化**了。
ostensible§The ostensible author never saw the manuscript.§**名义上**的作者从未见过这份手稿。
ostentatious§Ostentatious modesty is still ostentation.§**炫耀式**的谦逊仍然是炫耀。
oust§Water ousted air from the pipe with a sound like a cough.§水把管子里的空气**挤出去**，发出咳嗽般的声响。
outdated§An outdated form is still the only one the office accepts.§一份**过时**的表格仍是办公室唯一接受的。
outmode§Nothing outmodes a technology like a cheaper substitute.§没有什么比更便宜的替代品更能让一项技术**过时**。
outrage§Outrage is easy to generate and hard to sustain.§**愤怒**容易制造，难以维持。
overabundance§An overabundance of choice made the decision harder, not better.§选择**过多**让决定更难，而不是更好。
overhaul§The syllabus was overhauled and half the reading survived.§教学大纲被**彻底改造**，一半的书目留了下来。
overjoy§He was overjoyed and, twenty minutes later, exhausted.§他**欣喜若狂**，二十分钟后就精疲力尽。
overpower§The scent of the lilies overpowered the whole room.§百合的香气**压倒**了整个房间。
overshadow§A tall neighbour overshadows the garden all afternoon.§一栋高大的邻楼整个下午都**遮着**这座花园。
oversight§Parliamentary oversight of the fund began only in 1998.§议会对这笔基金的**监督**到一九九八年才开始。
overweening§Overweening ambition in a first novel is forgivable.§第一部小说里**过度的野心**是可以原谅的。
pacifist§Pacifist convictions cost him his job and not his friends.§**反战**的信念让他丢了工作，却没让他失去朋友。
painstaking§Painstaking work looks effortless, which is the problem.§**费尽心力**的工作看起来毫不费力，问题正在这里。
palliative§Palliative care is a specialty, not a surrender.§**姑息治疗**是一门专科，不是放弃。
palpable§The pulse was palpable at the wrist and nowhere else.§脉搏只在手腕处**摸得到**，别处都摸不到。
panache§He returned the serve with panache and lost the point.§他**潇洒**地回了一球，却输了这一分。
panoply§The full panoply of ceremony was reserved for the last day.§**全套的仪仗**只留给最后一天。
panoramic§A panoramic photograph flattens the very depth it shows.§**全景**照片把它所展示的纵深压平了。
pantomime§The whole exchange was a pantomime for the benefit of the press.§整场交流都是演给媒体看的**哑剧**。
paradigm§A paradigm changes when the anomalies stop being interesting.§当反常现象不再引人兴趣时，**范式**就改变了。
paradox§The paradox dissolves as soon as you define the term.§一旦定义清楚术语，这个**悖论**就消解了。
paragon§Held up as a paragon, she found the position exhausting.§被树为**楷模**，她觉得这个位置令人筋疲力尽。
paramount§What is paramount in June is forgotten by September.§六月**至关重要**的事，到九月就被忘了。
parch§Parched ground takes rain worse than damp ground does.§**干裂**的土地比湿润的土地更不吸水。
parochial§Parochial records begin in 1538 and are the best source we have.§**教区**记录始于一五三八年，是我们拥有的最佳史料。
parody§A parody that is kinder than the original misses its aim.§比原作还宽厚的**戏仿**就失去了目的。
partial§I am partial to the second version and I know why.§我**偏爱**第二个版本，也知道原因。
